mission.heading: We see you. We hear you. `And we are with you.`
paragraphs: EmpowerHer was born from the hope and strength that you carry within you—even in the darkest of days. You are not forgotten. Your dreams, your voices, your potential—they matter. They are powerful, and they are needed in this world.

We know that many of you are facing unimaginable challenges. Barriers to education, threats to your freedom, and a world that too often refuses to see your worth. But we believe in your resilience. And through EmpowerHer, we are building a path forward—together.

Our mission is simple: to support you, to uplift you, and to walk beside you. Whether through education, mentorship, leadership workshops, or simply being a voice when yours is silenced, we are here for you.
Please don't give up. There is a growing community—inside and outside Afghanistan—that believes in your power to lead, to learn, and to rise. And we are proud to stand with you.

hero.heading:
Born from lived experience.
Built for Afghan women.
hero.body: A movement dedicated to equipping Afghan women with resilience, creativity, and leadership to shine as sources of inspiration — even in the face of adversity.

cards.heading: Our Mission
cards.body: EmpowerHer focuses on equipping Afghan women to become beacons of hope in the darkest of times when the shadows of the Taliban seek to stifle the voices of Afghan women. By nurturing resilience, creativity, and leadership, we strive to empower them to shine as sources of inspiration and strength, uplifting their communities even in the face of adversity.

cards.heading: Our Vision
cards.body: We envision Afghan women as guiding lights in their communities, inspiring hope and progress while leading the way to a more equitable, inclusive, and sustainable society.

bodyBefore: EmpowerHer was born out of the lived experiences of its Co-Founders, Mahdi Rahimi and Nahid Karimi, both of whom were raised in Kabul, Afghanistan.

Growing up, they witnessed firsthand the deep-rooted inequalities and daily struggles Afghan communities — particularly women and girls — face. From societal restrictions to systemic educational barriers, the challenges were immense, but the desire to create change was even greater.
ourStory.pullQuote: “The fall of Kabul on August 15, 2021, marked a turning point — not only for their own lives but for the future of millions of Afghan girls who were suddenly stripped of their basic right to education.”
bodyAfter: With schools closed to girls over the age of 12 and women increasingly pushed out of public life, Mahdi and Nahid knew silence was not an option.

After resettling in the United States, they immediately began organizing virtual programs aimed at supporting Afghan youth — both men and women — inside Afghanistan and across the diaspora. These early efforts, though impactful, were limited in scope and duration. They reached small groups and operated with minimal resources, yet they revealed something powerful: the need was urgent, and the demand was growing.

It was from this realization that EmpowerHer emerged — not just as a project, but as a movement. A more comprehensive, organized, and sustainable platform was needed to continue this work on a larger scale. Founded and led by Afghan youth who understand the struggles of their own people, EmpowerHer stands today as a symbol of resilience, hope, and empowerment.

whatWeDo.heading: What We Do
whatWeDo.intro: Four interconnected pillars that work together to create lasting change for Afghan women.

pillars.title: Advocacy

pillars.title: Education & Leadership
pillars.description: Through skill-based workshops focused on leadership, personal development, communication, and decision-making, we equip Afghan girls with the confidence and tools to lead their communities with strength and purpose.

pillars.title: Creative Expression
pillars.description: We empower Afghan girls to reclaim their voices through writing, storytelling, and the arts. Our programs provide platforms for creative expression as a powerful form of resistance and healing, helping them share their lived experiences with the world.

pillars.title: Community Engagement
pillars.description: Our graduates and members can access EmpowerHer's resources and engage with our vibrant community. We support them in creating impactful initiatives both within and outside Afghanistan through virtual and in-person programs.

judgeTestimonials.title: What Our Judges Felt Reading These Stories

judges.name: Dr. Ellen Leggett
judges.title: Professor of Psychology and Founding Director of Applied Psychology Master’s Program (Retired), University of Southern California
judges.quote: It was an honor to read about and bear witness to the incredibly moving stories told by these writers. Many of us aspire to be courageous and to overcome adversity in our lives, and the writings of these Afghan women teach us all a humbling lesson. With elegant beauty and wisdom, the inspirational stories recounted by these writers demonstrate strength of character, love of learning, and the best of human persistence and resilience in the face of pain. A reverberating question stays with me: What feats would these remarkable women accomplish in a world that welcomed them? And the world does need them. Let their voices teach you.

judges.name: Dr. Susan M. Blaustein
judges.title: Instructor, Columbia University, Founder/Board Chair, WomenStrong International
judges.quote: My immediate impression, when reading the submissions, was that this body of work has been produced by an extraordinarily talented, capable, bold, and determined group of young women. I was deeply moved by their courage, grit, and refusal to be restrained in shadow and silence. These are young women who, like all young women and girls everywhere, have dreams, rights, and hopes for their futures, yet in far too many cruel places on earth, those dreams and rights are denied. I am honored to have worked closely with Afghan women and girls over the past seven years as they have repeatedly faced and overcome seemingly insurmountable challenges. We must continue to raise awareness of, and refuse to tolerate, this tremendous injustice, which threatens the future and promise of Afghanistan and stands in clear violation of the rights of women and girls.

judges.name: Dr. Sonia Palmieri
judges.title: Associate Professor, Department of Pacific Affairs, Australian National University
judges.quote: I was incredibly moved by the stories of bravery, confidence, tragedy and injustice shared by the Afghan artists. As an academic, creative writing is something I admire, perhaps in part because it is so difficult for me. But the huge response to the EmpowerHer writing competition shows that there is a wealth of creativity among Afghan women, and that writing can be a powerful way to process a range of both conflicting and complementary emotions — sadness, rage, frustration, joy. Certainly, the entrants wanted to share a profound sense of injustice at the hands of the Taliban. They did this with strong, pictorial clarity. Yet this was always underpinned by narratives of resilience and hope. Afghan women’s refusal of defeat in such conditions will change the world.

aboutContest.title: About the Contest
aboutContest.paragraph: EmpowerHer's HerVoice initiative aims to provide a space where Afghan girls can truly express their stories, feelings, and experiences freely. This contest is designed to reflect the realities Afghan girls and women are facing under the oppressive Taliban regime. Their educational, social, and economic lives have been shattered, and through this contest, we seek to share these narratives, commemorate the hardships Afghan girls and women continue to endure, and reward and recognize their resilience, courage, and motivation to push forward in the face of adversity.

judges.title: Our Judges

items.name: Dr. Susan M. Blaustein
items.description: Dr. Susan M. Blaustein is the Founding Board Chair and President of WomenStrong International, a global nonprofit that supports local feminist leaders advancing the rights of women and girls worldwide. She previously co-founded and directed the Millennium Cities Initiative at Columbia University's Earth Institute and has worked on conflict prevention and international justice with leading global organizations. A writer and journalist, she has reported on global politics and social justice for major publications including The New Yorker and The Wall Street Journal. Dr. Blaustein teaches at Columbia University's Climate School, holds a doctorate from Yale University, was a Harvard Junior Fellow, and has received numerous honors, including a Guggenheim Fellowship and the Ban Ki-moon Award for Women's Empowerment.

items.name: Dr. Ellen Leggett
items.description: Dr. Ellen Leggett is a psychologist with a lifelong passion for supporting the education of girls and women. She graduated from Mount Holyoke College, the first U.S. college founded for women, and was Associate Dean of Students at Scripps College, an esteemed California college for women. Most recently, she has been Professor of Psychology at the University of Southern California and Founding Director of the Master's in Applied Psychology program there, where she has taught students from all over the world. She holds master's and doctoral degrees in Human Development and Education from Harvard University.

items.name: Dr. Sonia Palmieri
items.description: Associate Professor Dr. Sonia Palmieri is Head of the Department of Pacific Affairs at the Coral Bell School of Asia and Pacific Affairs, Australian National University. Her research focuses on women's leadership in political institutions, particularly gender-sensitive parliaments. She is a leading contributor to both the theory and practice of inclusive and feminist research methodologies.

items.name: Dr. Marilyn Sides
items.description: Dr. Marilyn Sides is an Associate Teaching Professor in the Department of English and Creative Writing at Wellesley College, where she also serves as Director of Creative Writing. She is affiliated with the Comparative Literary Studies Program. Marilyn is the author of the short story collection The Island of the Mapmaker's Wife and the novel The Genius of Affection. At Wellesley, she teaches creative writing as well as literature courses.

items.name: Patrick M. Erwin
items.description: Patrick M. Erwin is the Curriculum Director at the Maxwell Leadership Foundation, with extensive experience in education and leadership development. He previously served 17 years as a high school band director in Cobb County, Georgia. Patrick holds degrees in Political Science, Music Education, and Leadership, and is an award-winning speaker who presents nationally on leadership, student engagement, and professional growth.

items.name: Andrew McPeak
items.description: Andrew McPeak is an author, researcher, and expert on emerging generations with over a decade of experience working with young adults across education and professional settings. He is the co-host of the School on a Mission Podcast, co-author of Marching off the Map (2017) and Generation Z Unfiltered (2019), and the author of Ready for Real Life (2023).

items.name: Bella Fisher
items.description: Bella Fisher is a junior at Miss Hall's School in Massachusetts and grew up on a farm in Berkshire County. She has a strong interest in creative writing and the arts, particularly prose and fiction, and enjoys exploring literary and artistic projects. She is an editor at the literary magazine Girls Write the World, where she helps amplify young voices through writing and editorial work. Bella is passionate about supporting other young writers and aspires to publish her own work in the future.

items.name: Maia Roberts
items.description: Maia Roberts is a junior at Miss Hall's School, where she pursues advanced coursework in English and history with a particular focus on feminist studies. Her academic work has earned her placement on the Head's List each semester of high school. She is an editor at the international literary journal Girls Right the World, where she contributes to elevating young voices through writing and editorial work. Maia believes in the importance of using literature and education to explore gender equity and amplify underrepresented perspectives.

items.name: Juliet Hopkins
items.description: Juliet Hopkins is a junior at Miss Hall's School and is originally from Rabun County, Georgia. She has a strong interest in creative writing and oil painting, and she balances her artistic pursuits with athletics as a varsity volleyball player. She is an editor at the literary magazine Girls Right the World, where she helps amplify young voices through writing and editorial work. Juliet believes in the importance of uplifting the voices of refugee girls and learning more about their experiences and backgrounds.

seo.description: Free workshops and mentorship for Afghan girls to build resilience, gain support, and launch impact projects.

hero.title: Mentorship
paragraphs: EmpowerHer's main program is the Mentorship Program, where students can apply to one of our workshops and receive free mentorship from our dedicated and highly trained mentors and lecturers.
This program aims to provide Afghan girls with the resources, opportunities, and networks they need to launch their own impact projects.

intro.quote: Through this platform, EmpowerHer encourages students to think outside the box and view their challenges as sources of resilience—life lessons that empower them to pursue their goals and dreams.
intro.paragraph: EmpowerHer creates a safe, supportive space where students can discuss their struggles openly, feel heard and seen, and reflect on their experiences.
intro.impactText: Whether through launching a project, mentoring a sibling or friend, or simply taking a first step, EmpowerHer helps students grow—one story, one action, and one empowered voice at a time.
intro.closing: Join us in empowering the next generation of Afghan leaders and changemakers through our comprehensive mentorship program.

workshopStructure.title: Workshop Structure
workshopStructure.description: Every detail is designed to maximize learning, connection, and empowerment.

items.title: Cycle Duration
items.description: Each workshop runs in 6-week cycles (about 1.5 months).

items.title: Sessions per Week
items.description: Workshops meet twice weekly — on Saturdays and Sundays.

items.title: Session Length
items.description: Each session is 2 hours long.

items.title: Saturday Sessions
items.description: Led by assigned mentors. Focused on skill-building, presentations, and guided activities.

items.title: Sunday Sessions
items.description: Dedicated to guest speaker presentations, group discussions, lecturers, and Q&A. Covers themes related to empowerment, leadership, storytelling, and resilience.

items.title: Workshop Format
items.description: Fully virtual via Google Meet. Materials including assignments and other activities are posted through separate Google Classrooms.

items.title: Participant Limit
items.description: Each workshop accepts 16 participants to ensure personalized attention.

items.title: Mentorship Style
items.description: Collaborative and discussion-based, encouraging peer support and active participation. Mentors guide students through both personal reflection and project development.

items.title: Project-Based Learning
items.description: Participants complete capstone or final projects such as creative writing, art, real-world projects, impact proposals, or cultural presentations reflecting what they have learned.

eligibility.title: Who Can Apply
eligibility.description: Please review the following requirements before applying to any EmpowerHer workshop.
rules: Afghan girls residing in Afghanistan and any other Middle Eastern or Central Asian countries are welcome to apply to our programs.
Intermediate or advanced English proficiency is required.
Although there is no age limit to apply to any of EmpowerHer's workshops, our team prefers applicants aged 14 and above.

Afghan girls residing in Europe or America (any region outside the Middle East and Central Asia) are not eligible to apply to our programs; however, we encourage them to volunteer with us through the following link: Volunteer
Men are not eligible to apply to our programs at this time.

seo.title: Student Project Roadmap — EmpowerHer Initiative
seo.description: A leadership pathway for EmpowerHer graduates to design and lead their own impact-driven online classes.

hero.heading: Student Project Roadmap (SPR)
hero.intro: The Student Project Roadmap (SPR) is a leadership pathway for EmpowerHer students who have completed their workshops and met eligibility requirements and wish to deepen their practical leadership experience. Through a structured, step-by-step process, students work closely with EmpowerHer's team to design and lead their own impact-driven online classes, directly advancing EmpowerHer's mission and expanding educational access for more Afghan girls.

eligibility.heading: Eligibility Requirements
eligibility.subtitle: Before applying, confirm you meet all three criteria below.
items: Students must successfully complete and obtain Certificates of Completion for two consecutive workshops.
Students must be actively engaged in the two workshops they attended and punctual with all assigned work, including discussions, projects, assignments, and other mentorship materials.
Students must pass an interview with the Mentorship Program Director assessing skillsets and language proficiency.

howToApply.title: How to Apply
howToApply.bodyAfter: . Include your full name, the two EmpowerHer workshops you have attended, and your reasons for wanting to join this roadmap. Once received, the Mentorship Program Director will schedule an interview shortly.

steps.title: Welcome as Assistant
steps.description: Successful candidates are welcomed as Assistants for two workshop cycles. We will match you with any available mentor and his/her respective workshop.

steps.title: Hands-On Experience
steps.description: Assistants gain hands-on experience supporting new participants and learning how an EmpowerHer workshop operates. They will learn about EmpowerHer's internal system, including training on how to check MIS applications, registration applications, communicate effectively, and lead online sessions.

steps.title: Design Your Workshop
steps.description: During these two workshop cycles, assistants design their own online workshops and prepare mentorship materials. All materials are subject to approval from EmpowerHer's Mentorship Program Director.

steps.title: Academic Demo Session
steps.description: Towards the end of Assistant training and the two month workshop cycle, assistants conduct a one and half hour long Academic Demo Session, mentoring a staff member (with their materials) to demonstrate their teaching and leadership skills.

steps.title: Promoted to Mentor
steps.description: After successfully completing the demo, Assistants are promoted to Mentor positions, officially joining the EmpowerHer Mentorship Program and mentoring many more Afghan girls.

items.title: Hands-On Leadership Experience
items.description: Gain practical skills in leading online classes and mentoring peers.

items.title: Professional Development
items.description: Learn how a nonprofit operates and develop communication, project management, and organizational skills.

items.title: Direct Impact
items.description: Expand educational access for Afghan girls through student-led initiatives.

items.title: Mentorship & Guidance
items.description: Receive structured support and feedback from EmpowerHer's experienced team throughout the roadmap.

items.title: Resource & Networking Opportunities

seo.title: Sisterhood Sessions — EmpowerHer Initiative
seo.description: A supportive and caring space for EmpowerHer students to connect, share ideas, and build friendships.

header.heading: Sisterhood Sessions
header.body: Sisterhood Sessions are designed to provide a supportive and caring space for all EmpowerHer students enrolled in the mentorship program. These sessions allow students to connect with one another, share their ideas, build friendships, and offer constructive feedback on EmpowerHer programs.

whyTheyMatter.heading: Why Sisterhood Sessions Matter
whyTheyMatter.body: Sisterhood Sessions were created in response to the loss of hope many girls and women in Afghanistan are experiencing due to restrictions on education and opportunity. EmpowerHer aims to provide not only educational support but also a space where students feel encouraged, heard, and valued.
whyTheyMatter.quote: During these sessions, EmpowerHer assistants support students with both personal challenges and workshop-related concerns. The conversations are designed to foster confidence, resilience, and hope as students continue advocating for their right to education and a better future.

community.heading: A Safe and Supportive Community
community.body: The purpose of Sisterhood Sessions is to help students build long-lasting relationships and create a safe space where they can openly share their thoughts, experiences, and life stories. Many of our students rarely have environments where they feel truly heard, respected, and supported.
community.listIntro: Through open conversations and peer connection, students can:
benefits: Discuss challenges they face in their daily lives
community.closing: These sessions help students develop stronger emotional well-being and a deeper sense of belonging within the EmpowerHer community.

sessionFormat.heading: Session Format

cards.title: When They Take Place
cards.body: Sisterhood Sessions take place at the end of each workshop session on Saturdays and Sundays.

cards.title: Session Duration
cards.body: Each Sisterhood Session lasts 30 minutes, providing dedicated time for connection and conversation.

sessionFormat.closing: These sessions ensure that every workshop not only focuses on learning and skill development but also prioritizes community, connection, and emotional support. By creating time for reflection and conversation, Sisterhood Sessions help students strengthen their relationships with one another and feel supported throughout their EmpowerHer journey.

seo.title: AGFAF — EmpowerHer Initiative
seo.description: Afghan Girls Financial Assistance Fund — our primary sponsor and partner.

logo.alt: AGFAF — Afghan Girls Financial Assistance Fund

agfaf.title: Afghan Girls Financial Assistance Fund (AGFAF)
description: The Afghan Girls Financial Assistance Fund (AGFAF) is a U.S.-based nonprofit organization dedicated to empowering young Afghan women through education. Founded in response to the systemic barriers Afghan girls face in accessing quality education, AGFAF works to identify, support, and sponsor talented students who demonstrate academic promise and leadership potential.

AGFAF partners with high schools, colleges, and universities across the United States to provide full financial aid, housing, and mentorship for Afghan girls who have limited or no access to education in their home country. In addition to academic support, AGFAF also offers guidance in college and career planning, cultural adjustment, and leadership development, helping these students become confident, educated changemakers within their communities and beyond.

The organization's mission is rooted in the belief that educating girls is one of the most powerful tools for creating lasting peace, gender equality, and economic growth in Afghanistan and the world.
AGFAF continues to grow as a network of scholars, educators, host families, and global advocates working together to ensure that Afghan girls have the opportunity to learn, lead, and thrive.

gratitude.title: Our Deepest Gratitude
gratitude.quote: EmpowerHer deeply values the unwavering support of the Afghan Girls Financial Assistance Fund (AGFAF). As our primary sponsor and partner, AGFAF has played a pivotal role in making many of our initiatives and programs possible. For nearly two decades, AGFAF has illuminated the path toward a brighter future for countless Afghan girls. As fellow Afghans and an organization aligned with their mission and vision, we extend our heartfelt gratitude for their continued support and belief in our work.

seo.title: Monthly Internet Scholarship (MIS) — EmpowerHer Initiative
seo.description: EmpowerHer provides monthly internet scholarships to help members participate in our programs.

content.heading: Monthly Internet Scholarship (MIS)
body: EmpowerHer provides Monthly Internet Scholarships (MIS) to all students who need them most, helping them participate fully in our programs. We understand the financial challenges many girls face in Afghanistan and how difficult it can be to access reliable internet. That's why we're proud to offer this financial support and ensure that access to learning is not limited by financial barriers.

Please note: EmpowerHer does not send funds through "Hawala" or any platform that allows cash withdrawal. Instead, we provide internet credit through the Ding application, which lets students activate any internet bundles they need. Also, Ding and our system do not support Salam SIM cards, so please do not include Salam numbers in your MIS or workshop registration forms.
content.advisory: Please be advised that EmpowerHer provides MIS exclusively to students formally accepted into its programs. This support is not available to individuals outside EmpowerHer or to those currently attending virtual or in-person programs offered by other organizations.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: This Privacy Policy describes how EmpowerHer collects, uses, and protects participant information across its programs, workshops, publications, and platforms.
privacy.body:
EmpowerHer is committed to protecting the privacy of the Afghan women and girls who participate in its programs. This Privacy Policy describes the information we collect, how we use it, and the choices and protections available to participants across our programs, workshops, publication platforms, scholarships, events, and initiatives.

## Information We Collect

EmpowerHer may collect information including:

- Names
- Email addresses
- Application materials
- Educational information
- Workshop participation records
- Submitted writings and creative works

## How We Use Your Information

Information collected may be used for:

- Program administration
- Workshop coordination
- Scholarship review
- Publication opportunities
- Communication regarding EmpowerHer activities

## Confidentiality

EmpowerHer will protect participant information and will not share personal data with third parties without consent, except when necessary for program administration or improvement of program operations. EmpowerHer is not responsible for unauthorized disclosure, sharing, or misuse of program materials or participant information by third parties or participants.

Participants should avoid sharing sensitive personal information during public workshops, events, or publications.

## Media and Publication Consent

By participating in EmpowerHer programs and voluntarily submitting written work, photographs, or creative projects, participants grant EmpowerHer permission to:

- Publish submitted work on EmpowerHer platforms.
- Share participant achievements and success stories.
- Promote EmpowerHer programs through websites, newsletters, reports, and social media.

## Data Retention and Security

EmpowerHer implements reasonable safeguards to protect participant data and retains information only as long as necessary for program administration and reporting purposes.

## Modifications

- EmpowerHer reserves the right to modify this Privacy Policy at any time. Updated policies will be posted on official EmpowerHer platforms.
- Continued participation in EmpowerHer programs constitutes acceptance of this policy.

## Contact Us

If you have questions about this Privacy Policy or our practices, contact us at:

**EmpowerHer Initiative**  
Email: [info@empowerher-initiative.org](mailto:info@empowerher-initiative.org)

seo.title: Terms — EmpowerHer Initiative
seo.description: These Terms and Policies describe the terms and conditions for participating in EmpowerHer programs, workshops, publications, scholarships, events, and initiatives.

terms.title: Terms
terms.description: These Terms and Policies describe the terms and conditions for participating in EmpowerHer programs, workshops, publications, scholarships, events, and initiatives.
terms.body:
EmpowerHer is committed to creating educational, mentorship, leadership, and publication opportunities for Afghan women and girls in the safest and most efficient ways possible. By participating in any EmpowerHer program, workshop, publication platform, scholarship program, event, or initiative, participants agree to comply with the following terms and policies.

## General Community Guidelines

All EmpowerHer participants, including students, mentors, lecturers, volunteers, staff members, and contributors, are expected to:

- Treat all members of the EmpowerHer community with respect, dignity, and kindness.
- Maintain a safe, inclusive, and supportive learning environment.
- Refrain from harassment, discrimination, or harmful conduct.
- Respect the privacy and confidentiality of other participants.
- Communicate respectfully during workshops, meetings, online discussions, and other EmpowerHer activities and programs.
- Uphold EmpowerHer's mission of empowering Afghan women and girls through education, leadership, storytelling, and advocacy.

EmpowerHer maintains a zero-tolerance policy for violations of these guidelines. Participants who violate these policies may be removed from programs, workshops, or other EmpowerHer opportunities.

## Mentorship Program Policies

### Attendance

- Students are expected to attend all workshop sessions.
- Students may miss only one workshop session during a workshop round (exclusively a Sunday session).
- Missing more than one session may result in disqualification from receiving a certificate of completion.
- Students should notify their mentors or workshop assistants in advance if they are unable to attend a session. Reasonable exceptions may be granted for extenuating circumstances.

### Assignments

- All assignments must be completed and submitted before the stated deadlines.
- Students who fail to submit more than two assignments may be disqualified from receiving a certificate of completion.
- Assignments are evaluated as Complete or Incomplete.
- EmpowerHer maintains a strict no-AI policy across all Mentorship Program workshops and initiatives. The use of AI tools for assignments or activities is prohibited.

### Conduct

- Students must follow all workshop-specific expectations established by mentors.
- Mentors reserve the right to remove students who repeatedly violate EmpowerHer policies or disrupt the learning environment.
- Academic honesty is expected in all submitted work.
- Students must treat fellow students and EmpowerHer staff with respect at all times, including during discussions and disagreements.

## HerVoice Publication Policies

### Eligibility

- Contributors must be active participants in EmpowerHer programs, particularly the Creative Writing and Storytelling Workshop.
- All submissions must align with EmpowerHer's mission and values.

### Content Guidelines

- Writers must carefully revise and edit their work before submission.
- First drafts and unfinished pieces may be rejected.
- Submissions should focus on a single topic, prompt, or theme.
- Writing should reflect personal experiences, perspectives, creativity, or issues connected to EmpowerHer's mission.
- Language should be respectful, appropriate, and free from harmful content.

### Images

- Every submission must include a photo, artwork, or illustration.
- AI-generated images are not permitted.
- If an image is obtained from another source, proper credit and the original link must be provided.

### Word Limits

- Essays, articles, stories, and fiction pieces: Maximum 1,000 words.
- Poems: Maximum 40 lines.

### Originality and AI Policy

- The use of generative artificial intelligence tools (including ChatGPT and similar platforms) for writing submissions is prohibited.
- All submitted work must be the author's original work.
- Submissions suspected of substantial AI generation may be rejected.

### Author Biography

- Writers must include a short biography of no more than 150 words.
- Providing social media links is optional.

### Editorial Rights

- EmpowerHer reserves the right to edit submissions for grammar, formatting, clarity, and publication standards.
- Submission does not guarantee publication.
- EmpowerHer reserves the right to decline submissions that do not meet publication standards or align with its mission.
- Copyright in the Work remains vested in the Author, who is responsible for ensuring that the Work does not infringe upon the rights of any third party.

## Monthly Internet Scholarship Policies

### Eligibility

- Applicants must be active participants in EmpowerHer programs.
- Applicants must demonstrate consistent participation and engagement.
- Priority may be given to students who demonstrate financial need through their MIS application, as well as strong attendance, assignment completion, and active involvement within the EmpowerHer community throughout their workshop cycle.

### Expectations

- Scholarship recipients are expected to use the support primarily for educational purposes.
- Recipients should maintain active participation in EmpowerHer programs.
- Students must communicate honestly regarding their educational and financial needs.
- Receiving a scholarship does not guarantee future funding.

## Modifications

- EmpowerHer reserves the right to modify these terms, policies, and program requirements at any time. Updated policies will be posted on official EmpowerHer platforms.
- Continued participation in EmpowerHer programs constitutes acceptance of these policies.

## Legal Protections and Compliance

1. EmpowerHer is not liable for any direct or indirect loss, harm, or damages arising from participation in its programs, workshops, publications, or use of its platforms.
2. Participants agree to indemnify and hold EmpowerHer harmless from any claims, damages, or liabilities arising from submitted work or participation, including but not limited to copyright infringement or violations of third-party rights.
3. By submitting work for publication, participants grant EmpowerHer a non-exclusive, royalty-free, and perpetual license to publish, reproduce, and distribute the submitted content across its platforms.
4. EmpowerHer implements reasonable safeguards to protect participant data and retains information only as long as necessary for program administration and reporting purposes.
5. Violations of EmpowerHer policies, including academic misconduct, use of prohibited AI tools, or disruptive behavior, may result in disqualification, removal from programs, or revocation of certificates or benefits.
6. Organizations may verify the validity of certificates issued to EmpowerHer staff, volunteers, and students by contacting [info@empowerher-initiative.org](mailto:info@empowerher-initiative.org).

## Contact Us

If you have questions about these Terms and Policies, contact us at:

**EmpowerHer Initiative**  
Email: [info@empowerher-initiative.org](mailto:info@empowerher-initiative.org)
